                      LINK N3 OPPOSITION LANDOWNERS’ INITIAL BRIEF

            Pursuant to SOAH Order No. 6, JHET Ranch, LLC (JHET Ranch), JCS Ranch, LLC and

  Johnny Sandlin (JCS Ranch), Angell Land and Livestock, LLC (Angell Land), Kaddo and Penni

  Kothmann (the Kothmanns), MK3 Investments, LLC (MK3 Investments), Carl S. Menzies,

  Trustee of the Menzies Residual Trust (Menzies Trust), and Rancho Bonito Livestock Company

  (Ranch Bonito) (collectively, Link N3 Opposition Landowners), timely file this Initial Brief on or

  before June 19, 2026. Along with this initial brief, the Link N3 Opposition Landowners incorporate

  by reference the initial brief of Save the Lampasas 25, Inc. (Save the Lampasas) and kindly request

  the SOAH ALJs first read the arguments in that brief before turning to the instant initial brief.1


                                                I.        INTRODUCTION

           Link N3 Opposition Landowners oppose any route that contains Link N3, which includes

  the route the Joint Applicants have identified as the “best meets” route, Route 894, as that link


           1
              For the purposes of judicial economy, the Link N3 Opposition Landowners incorporate by reference all the
  arguments made by Save the Lampasas in its initial brief. As the Link N3 Opposition Landowners are on the western
  half of the study area near the existing Big Hill substation, it files a separate brief to address arguments that only apply
  to the Link N3 Opposition Landowners.
                                                                                          Page 3 of 17


does not comply with the routing criteria. Link N3 affects numerous habitable structures, fails to

follow property lines and existing transmission lines, and presents strong community value

concerns, among other issues. Overall, Link N3 Opposition Landowners strongly believe that

Route 572, Route 276, or any other route utilizing Link N4 or N12,2 best addresses the routing

criteria found in 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B) and PURA § 37.056. Other routes that are reasonable

alternatives to Route 894, based on the record in this case and the routing criteria, include any

route that does not include Link N3.3


       While Link N3 is used in Route 894, it is not used in any of the other Routes of Interest

except for Route 891.4 The use of N4 or N12 in routes is superior to that of N3. Both from a link

and routing perspective, using N4 or N12 better addresses community values from an intervention

and land use perspective. Link N4 is also a superior choice from a paralleling standpoint.

Furthermore, using Link N12 is better than using N3 in terms of cost, environmental integrity, and

an aesthetics perspective. Using either link better addresses the Commission’s standard of prudent

avoidance. The choice of N3 in the use of Route 894 and other routes occurs because of the routing

corridors and the limited routing choices in this application, not as a result of Link N3 better

addressing the Commission’s routing criteria.

                                         II.      ROUTING CRITERIA

   A. ALTERNATIVE ROUTE OPTIONS

   1. Limitations of Routing Corridors

        The Joint Applicant’s routing witness, Ms. Casey Petty prepared a routing memorandum

regarding the evaluation of the alternative routes.5 This routing memorandum discussed how Ms.

Petty “initially identified five alternative route links that created corridors in which to group

potential alternative routes.”6 The memorandum continued that using these links, five routing

corridors were identified.7 The three central routing corridors are identified by Links J12, J24, and

J27.8 However, as shown below, the three central routing corridors converge near J13, J4, and

K11.9




        The convergence of these central routing corridors means that five corridors only exist in

the middle of the Study Area. This changes as noted at the hearing on the merits in the western

Study Area near the existing Big Hill substation.11 One of these routing corridors in the western

section of the Study Area is governed by Link R1, which as noted by the Joint Applicants is on 95

of the 122 filed routes.12


        The result of the choice of routing corridors and the number of routes containing Link R1

limits the routing choices to only one central corridor in the western portion of the Study Area. For

instance, the choice of R1 mostly leads to the choice of Link P2 as noted by the fact that it is on

92 of the filed 122 routes.13 Once P2-R1 is chosen, N12 cannot be chosen since that is not a forward

progressing route.14 Similarly, once P2-R1 is chosen, P42 cannot be chosen, effectively limiting

the routing choices to N3 or N4.15 Therefore, by having the majority of the filed routes use the

combination of P2-R1, makes it almost certain that the central corridor is utilized for routes, and

extremely likely that N3 is chosen for routing choices. Instead, replacing N3 with N4 or N12 using

a combination of links discussed below would better address the routing criteria.

   B. COMMUNITY VALUES

“requires consideration of values and resources essential to a local community[,]”18 which includes

an assessment of comments from community leaders and members of the public.19 Cherokee Creek

   G. CULTURAL, AESTHETIC, AND HISTORICAL VALUES

       The Commission must also consider how a proposed route affects the cultural, aesthetic,

and historical values of a given area.77


       As noted above in the Community Values section, the aesthetics of routing the transmission

line along Link N12 is more consistent with the wind farms along that link and in Concho County,

Texas.78 Furthermore, Link N3 would be visible from home on JHET Ranch and cross the main

entrance of the ranch so that one would need to drive under the transmission line to access the

property.79 It is also in direct line sight of the main house on JCS Ranch where family and friends

congregate at the fire pit and BBQ pavilion.80


       Routes using N3, N12, or N4 perform similarly regarding cultural resources. For example,

Route 296 has 4 cultural resource sites crossed by the route, Route 894 and 894 Western Mod 1

both have 2 cultural resource sites cross by the route, and Route 894 Western Mod. Routes 296,

894, and 894 Western Mod 1 have 18, 12, and 19 recorded cultural resources within 1,000 feet of

the route centerline.81 However, as noted in the EA, “[t]he overall site density and diversity indicate

high archaeological sensitivity within the project area and support the likelihood of encountering

additional unrecorded cultural resources during future investigations.”82

                   III.   SUMMARY OF ROUTING RECOMMENDATIONS

       Overall, the Commission should select a route that uses N4 or N12 instead of N3, including

Route 296, as the route that best meets the routing criteria in PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B). As shown above, the selection of routes using N4 and N12 perform better from

a community values, cost, paralleling, and prudent avoidance perspective. Routes that contain N4

and N12 also perform similarly regarding cultural and environmental factors as those routes that

contain N3. Significant evidence and testimony has been put forward regarding other portions of

the study area and Link N3 Opposition Landowners takes no position as to the routing alternatives

in those portions of the study area.


                                       IV.   CONCLUSION

       For the reasons stated in this Initial Brief, Link N3 Opposition Landowners recommend

that the ALJs recommend that the Commission any route that does not include Link N3.

Additionally, Link N3 Opposition Landowners respectfully request any other relief to which it has

shown itself entitled.

                   III.    SUMMARY OF ROUTING RECOMMENDATIONS

       Overall, the Commission should select a route that uses N4 or N12 instead ofN3, including

Route 296, as the route that best meets the routing criteria in PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC §

25.101(b)(3)(B). As shown above, the selection of routes using N4 and N12 perform better from

a community values, cost, paralleling, and prudent avoidance perspective. Routes that contain N4

and N12 also perform similarly regarding cultural and environmental factors as those routes that

contain N3. Significant evidence and testimony has been put forward regarding other portions of

the study area and Link N3 Opposition Landowners takes no position as to the routing alternatives

in those portions of the study area.
